sections.heading: Which Blue Lock Farm Code Should You Redeem First?
paragraphs: All five codes are free and none of them conflict, so the honest answer is: if they are all still listed above, redeem all of them. Each one tops up a different part of your account, and none of the rewards overlap enough to make one a bad pick.
That said, if you are prioritising by what your account needs right now, this is how the current codes map to goals:
bullets: Want Trait Tokens → TRAITS (25) or ADMINABUSE (20)
Want Grade Tokens → ADMINABUSE (20) or WEATHER (5)
Want a Jackpot Token → POLISHER (1)

sections.heading: Why a Blue Lock Farm Code May Not Work
paragraphs: If a code from the table above fails, run through these checks before assuming it has expired:
bullets: Typos and extra spaces are the most common problem. Copy and paste the code exactly as shown and remove any leading or trailing spaces before pressing Redeem.
Each code can normally only be redeemed once per account. If you have already used a code, it will not grant rewards again.
A newly released code may not work on a server that was started before the code went live — rejoin a fresh server and try again.
Codes attached to an update or event can be retired at any time. If a code has expired, there is no way to redeem it retroactively — watch for replacements in the next update.

sections.heading: What Blue Lock Farm Code Rewards Do
paragraphs: The current codes hand out several different resource types, and knowing what each one does helps you decide which codes matter most for your account. Trait Tokens are the trait-related resource, Grade Tokens are used for player grading at the Ranking stand in the Plaza, and the Jackpot Token works with the game's jackpot-style locker reward system.

Potions support those same systems: Cash Potions boost your money, Grade Speed Potions affect grading, and Luck Potions affect luck. The ADMINABUSE code also includes a Variant Token, a separate reward type listed in the table above.
Our token guides explain each currency in detail, including how to earn more of them beyond the current codes.

sections.heading: How to Redeem the ADMINABUSE Code

It is also worth making a spending decision deliberately rather than immediately: 45 Trait Tokens from codes is a meaningful budget, and the trait interface in the live game shows exactly what is available to you at your current roster. If you ever cannot find the trait system after an update, check the live in-game interface rather than older guides — the game changes quickly.

In practice this means a stack of one token type does not spend like another: check what each balance is for before deciding which code to prioritise.

hero.heading: Blue Lock Farm Grade Tokens
hero.lead: Grade Tokens are used for player grading at the Ranking stand in the Plaza — and codes hand out 25 of them for free right now.

sections.heading: What Do Grade Tokens Do?
paragraphs: Grade Tokens are Blue Lock Farm's currency for player grading. Grading is one of the main ways to push an existing unit beyond what lockers and cash upgrades offer, which makes Grade Tokens a progression currency rather than a cosmetic one.

Grading sits alongside the rest of the improvement loop: you unlock units from lockers, place them to generate money, and then decide how much of your budget flows into grading. Because grades touch the units you already own, Grade Tokens tend to matter most once your roster has settled and you are refining your best members rather than adding new ones.

sections.heading: Where to Use Grade Tokens
paragraphs: Grading happens at the Ranking stand in the Plaza. The full flow looks like this:

steps.heading: Go to the Plaza
steps.description: The Ranking stand is located in the Plaza area of the map.

steps.heading: Find the Ranking stand
steps.description: Walk up to the stand to open its interface.

steps.heading: Select the player or unit you want to grade
steps.description: Pick the roster member whose grade you want to roll.

steps.heading: Choose the roll and pay
steps.description: Ranking rolls accept Grade Tokens or cash — pick whichever balance you want to spend and confirm the roll.

sections.heading: How to Get Grade Tokens
paragraphs: The fastest free source right now is code redemption. Two of the five current codes include Grade Tokens:

WEATHER grants 5 Grade Tokens plus 1 Luck Potion, and ADMINABUSE grants 20 Grade Tokens alongside 20 Trait Tokens and 1 Variant Token. That is 25 free Grade Tokens available to any account that redeems both codes.

To redeem, open the Shop on the left side of the screen, scroll to the code field, paste the code, and press Redeem. Codes change with every update, and a code that grants Grade Tokens today can expire after the next patch — the codes page always carries the current list and the date it was last checked.

sections.heading: Grade Tokens vs Cash Rolls
paragraphs: The Ranking stand accepts either Grade Tokens or cash for ranking rolls, and the two options trade off differently. Cash is always available — it comes from your placed characters and offline progression — so you can keep rolling as long as your farm income supports it.

The catch is cost escalation: repeated cash rolls on high-tier units can become very expensive, and cash spent on grading competes directly with lockers and upgrades in your budget. Grade Tokens sidestep that cost entirely, which is exactly why the 25 free tokens from codes are worth redeeming before you commit large amounts of cash.

sections.heading: When to Spend Grade Tokens
paragraphs: A reasonable pattern is to let your locker loop fund itself first. Place every character you unlock, keep upgrades going so your income grows, and treat Grade Tokens as a targeted investment rather than a default spend. Because repeated cash rolls get expensive at higher tiers, free tokens are best saved for the units you actually plan to keep long-term.
Also recheck the codes page before any big grading session. If a new code has added Grade Tokens to the reward pool, a few seconds of redemption can save you a large cash outlay.

sections.heading: Common Problems
bullets: Cannot find the Ranking stand: confirm you are in the Plaza; if a recent update changed things, rejoin the game and inspect the live Ranking stand UI.
Code redeemed but no tokens: check that the code granted Grade Tokens rather than a different reward — COMMUNITY, for example, grants potions, not Grade Tokens.
Ranking rolls feel expensive: repeated rolls on high-tier units cost escalating cash, which is why token-funded rolls are preferred.
Codes not working: recheck the code for typos and spaces, rejoin a fresh server, and confirm the code has not expired since your last visit.

title: Blue Lock Farm Lockers Guide – How Lockers Work
description: How Blue Lock Farm lockers work: opening Blue Lockers to unlock characters, the locker-to-income loop, and when to buy a better locker.
searchIntent: Players want to understand how the locker system works in Blue Lock Farm and how it drives progression.

hero.heading: Blue Lock Farm Lockers Guide
hero.lead: Lockers are Blue Lock Farm's core progression engine: open Blue Lockers to unlock characters, place them to earn money, and buy better lockers for rarer characters.

sections.heading: How Blue Lock Farm Lockers Work
paragraphs: Blue Lockers are the game's core way to unlock characters. Opening a locker adds roster members you can place on your farm — and the official game description is explicit about the second half of the system: buying better lockers gives you a chance at stronger and rarer characters.

That makes lockers both a starting point and a long-term goal. Early on, the lockers you can open set the ceiling on how strong your roster can get. As your income grows, saving for the next locker tier is the main way to raise that ceiling, because higher-tier characters earn more once they are placed.

sections.heading: Locker-to-Income Progression Loop
paragraphs: The whole game hangs on one loop that connects lockers to your income:

Open lockers to unlock characters. Place those characters so they generate money. Upgrade characters to boost their earnings. Reinvest the cash into better lockers, which offer a chance at stronger and rarer characters — and those characters, once placed, generate even more money. Your farm also climbs the leaderboard as your team grows, per the official description.

Every system in Blue Lock Farm feeds this loop. Tokens add a refinement layer on top of it, but the locker-to-income cycle is what compounds your farm's output over time. If you are ever unsure what to do next, the answer is almost always somewhere in this cycle.

links.label: Grade Tokens guide
links.description: How grading improves the characters your lockers produce.

sections.heading: When to Buy a Better Locker
paragraphs: The official description frames better lockers as a chance at stronger and rarer characters — a chance, not a guarantee. That framing matters for your spending decisions: a better locker is an investment in your roster's ceiling, while cheap lockers keep adding roster depth.

A reasonable trigger is income-based. When your placed characters are earning comfortably and upgrades have stopped moving the needle much, that surplus is exactly what the next locker tier is for. Buying better lockers too early starves your upgrades; buying them too late leaves your earnings capped by a roster you have already maxed out.

sections.heading: Upgrade or Open Another Locker?
paragraphs: Upgrades and lockers compete for the same cash, so it helps to think of them as different bets. Upgrades boost the earnings of characters you already own — a reliable, immediate improvement to your income. New lockers add characters you do not own yet, with better lockers offering the chance at rarer, higher-earning members.

A safe early-game default is to prioritise upgrades: a small roster gains a lot from each earnings boost, and stronger income makes every later locker purchase arrive sooner. Once your roster is placed and upgraded, shifting spending toward lockers keeps the loop growing. Token rewards from codes can also stretch this phase — free resources from the codes page reduce how much cash you need for either path.

links.label: Working codes
links.description: Free tokens and potions that ease the cash squeeze.

sections.heading: How Offline Earnings Fit the Loop
paragraphs: The official game description is direct about offline progression: lockers open and money generates while you are offline. In practice, this turns every login into a reinvestment window rather than a grind session.

The pattern that works with offline progression is simple: before you stop playing, make sure your characters are placed and your upgrades are current, because that setup keeps working while you are gone. When you come back, collect what your farm generated and immediately reinvest into the loop — another locker, more upgrades, or grading at the Ranking stand. Players who set up their roster before logging off tend to compound much faster than players who leave income idle.

sections.heading: Mistakes That Slow Progression
bullets: Leaving unlocked characters unplaced. Unplaced characters earn nothing — placement is free money.
Ignoring upgrades while chasing new lockers. Upgrades are the reliable income boost that funds your next locker.
Buying a better locker the moment you can afford it, then having no cash for upgrades. Better lockers are a chance at rarer characters, so time them against your income.
Skipping codes. Free tokens and potions from codes cover costs that would otherwise come straight out of your locker budget.
Not rechecking after updates. The game changes frequently, and new codes or mechanics can shift what the smart next purchase is.

sections.heading: New Codes and Token Changes
paragraphs: The late-September wave is the clearest signal yet that tokens are becoming Blue Lock Farm's main improvement currencies. Three of the five current codes hand out specialised tokens rather than potions, and the Jackpot Token from POLISHER is a resource class of its own.

This matters for how you plan spending. Cash still funds the locker-and-upgrade loop, but grading can now be covered largely by code rewards — so the smart play after each update is to redeem everything first, then decide what your cash should buy. The token guides below explain what each new currency does.

sections.heading: What Changes After an Update
paragraphs: Blue Lock Farm's updates tend to touch the same pressure points: the code list, token sources and reward mechanics. Codes added around a patch can retire older ones, so a code that worked last week may be gone today — and the first minutes after an update are the best time to grab whatever is new.

A routine that works well: redeem the new codes first, then spend a minute in the systems you actually use — the Shop's code box, the Ranking stand, and the jackpot/locker reward interface — so you are working from the live game rather than memory. Playing your first session after an update with the codes page open is the fastest way to catch everything that changed.

sections.heading: Where to Check Official Changes
paragraphs: The authoritative source for Blue Lock Farm news is the game's official page on Roblox, maintained by developer Finding Illusions. Updates, events and new codes are announced through the game page and its community channels.

This page sits between official announcements and your play sessions: it turns each confirmed change into a dated entry that explains what it means for your roster. When something here and the game disagree, the game wins — and the entry gets corrected.

faq.question: What is the latest Blue Lock Farm update?
faq.answer: The most recent confirmed activity is the late-September 2026 update wave, which added the codes TRAITS and ADMINABUSE around September 28, 2026, alongside POLISHER, COMMUNITY and WEATHER earlier in the window.

faq.question: What new codes were added to Blue Lock Farm recently?
faq.answer: TRAITS (25 Trait Tokens) and ADMINABUSE (20 Trait Tokens, 20 Grade Tokens, 1 Variant Token) were added around September 28, 2026, joining POLISHER, COMMUNITY and WEATHER from the same launch window.

faq.question: How often does Blue Lock Farm update?
faq.answer: There is no fixed schedule. The official Roblox page pushes game and community updates continuously, and new codes tend to arrive in bursts around patches and events.

faq.question: Do old codes stop working after a Blue Lock Farm update?
faq.answer: They can. Update and event codes can be retired at any time, so redeem working codes as soon as they appear and recheck the list after every patch.

faq.question: Where can I check official Blue Lock Farm news?
faq.answer: The game's official page on Roblox and Finding Illusions' community channels are the authoritative sources for updates and new codes.
